nodes.name: N-doped Co3O4@C on NF via mineralization-carbonization
nodes.procedure: Phase-transited lysozyme film adsorbed on NF substrate (PTL@NF) through immersion method, followed by biomimetic mineralization to grow Co3O4 nanosheets (Co3O4@PTL@NF), then carbonized to form N-doped Co3O4 wrapped in carbon mesh (N-Co3O4@C@NF).

unit_operations.name: Immersion
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: phase-transited lysozyme film to be adsorbed on the NF substrate (PTL@NF) through a facile immersion method

unit_operations.name: Biomimetic mineralization
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: 2D Co3O4 nanosheets were nucleated and grown on PTL@NF (Co3O4@PTL@NF)

unit_operations.name: Carbonization
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: finally carbonized to transform into the N-doped Co3O4 wrapped in carbon mesh

nodes.name: NiFe-OH NS/NF co-precipitation
nodes.procedure: Sun et al. proposed a one-step room temperature co-precipitation strategy, in which redox reaction took place accompanied with hydrolysis, to prepare Ni-Fe hydroxide nanosheet arrays supported on NF (NiFe-OH NS/NF). In detail, the pre-cleaned bare NF was immersed into 100 mm Fe(NO3)3·9H2O aqueous solution for 7 h, during which, a redox reaction between NF and Fe3+, as well as hydrolysis, occurred. Consequently, the generated Ni2+, Fe2+/Fe3+, and OH- co-precipitated to form even NiFe-OH nanosheet arrays on NF.
nodes.source_text: Figure 11g,h. Schematic illustration of synthetic procedure for NiFe-OH NS/NF.

nodes.name: NS-MnO2 hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: Zhang et al. reported that by immersing a cleaned NF substrate into KMnO4 solution under moderate hydrothermal conditions (at 180°C for 3 h), the desired ultrathin manganese dioxide nanosheet arrays in situ grown on the NF (denoted as NS-MnO2) can be fabricated.
nodes.source_text: Zhang et al. reported that by immersing a cleaned NF substrate into KMnO4 solution under moderate hydrothermal conditions (at 180°C for 3 h).
